messages:
liam: Heads-up — after landing the kernel-routing change yesterday we're seeing a regression on medium-length chat flows (seq_len ~512, batch 8). p50 token latency up ~18% when paged attention + interleaved KV are chosen. digging in now.
sophia: ack. do you have the perf numbers and which kernels got picked? sounds like routing preferred fused-flash for those shapes?
liam: root: routing favored fused_flash_v2 for many requests. quick numbers from local repro (A100):
```
baseline (flash_v1, separate-kv, fp16): p50 21.4ms, p95 46.7ms, throughput 210 tok/s
after routing change (fused_flash_v2, interleaved-kv, fp16): p50 25.2ms, p95 58.1ms, throughput 175 tok/s
```
rahul: interesting. fused_flash_v2 should be faster for long heads/big batch, but maybe our stride/layout assumptions broke cache behavior. did you check L2/SM occupancy and memory bandwidth?
liam: yes, perf counters show higher global load stalls and lower achieved bw with interleaved layout. suggests non-coalesced accesses when page boundaries misalign. also saw lots of small memcpy in the paged-attn path.
anya: can you paste the KV layout code snippet used for interleaved? I want to see the stride/alignment.
liam: snippet:
```
// interleaved layout: [batch, head, seq, dim_per_head]
kv_stride = align(dim_per_head, 64) // previously 64
page_offset = (seq_idx / page_size) * page_stride + (seq_idx % page_size) * kv_stride
```
sophia: a few thoughts:
- alignment 64 might be too big when dim_per_head is small (e.g., 64 -> aligned 64 fine, but when dim_per_head 32 we pad a lot).
- paged attention does an extra gather per page; combined with interleaved padding that could explode loads.
- dtype: are these fp16 or bf16? mixed dtype math changes kernel path.
liam: all tests in fp16. i also tried bf16 and saw similar pattern but slightly higher p50 (bf16 math slower on this hw). int8 path not in routing yet.
rahul: let's try two quick experiments: (1) same kernel routing but force separate KV layout, (2) keep interleaved but reduce alignment to 32 or use tight packing. that'll tell us if it's layout or kernel itself.
liam: ran both:
```
forced separate-kv + fused_flash_v2: p50 22.0ms, p95 48.0ms, throughput 205 tok/s
interleaved + alignment=32 + fused_flash_v2: p50 23.1ms, p95 50.2ms, throughput 195 tok/s
```
anya: so layout is the dominant factor. separate KV nearly recovers baseline. good signal.
ci-bot: CI perf-check completed for PR #4128 — gateway: regression detected (p50 token latency +15% on scenario: chat/medium-512). See run: https://ci.redwood/4128
rahul: ok two followups: (A) routing fallback: add a cost-model check that prefers separate-kv when seq_len in [128,1024] and dim_per_head <= 64; (B) kernel teams: evaluate fused_flash_v2 memory access pattern for interleaved padding cases.
liam: i've prototyped (A). added a cheap heuristic to the router: if predicted mem_loads > threshold prefer separate-kv variant. no CPU overhead. patch next.
sophia: for (B) we should add microbench where dim_per_head varies (16,32,64,128), page_size 32/64, alignment 16/32/64 and record global_load_stalls and cache-misses. include both fp16/bf16.
anya: I'll own the microbench. plan: matrix runs across three kernels: flash_v1, fused_flash_v2, paged_attention. record p50/p95, achieved BW, gld_stalls. upload CSV to perf bucket.
liam: thanks. one more oddity — for small batches (1-2) fused_flash_v2 still helps short seqs. so we shouldn't switch it off globally. router needs to be shape-aware.
rahul: agreed. make routing cost-model include batch size, seq_len, dim_per_head and KV layout overhead. simple linear model first, tune with microbench data.
ci-bot: perf matrix job queued: perf/matrix/attn-layout-2026-03-17. Estimated runtime 2h.
anya: kicked off the matrix, will share results. quick snippet of experiment plan:
```
shards=(flash_v1 fused_flash_v2 paged_attn)
for s in ${shards[@]}; do for dim in 16 32 64 128; do for page in 32 64; do run_bench --kernel $s --dim $dim --page $page --alignment 16,32,64 --dtype fp16,bf16; done; done; done
```
sophia: once we have CSV let's fit a tiny regression and export simple thresholds for router. also consider a conservative safety margin to avoid flip-flopping.
liam: action items:
- anya: run matrix + upload CSV (owner)
- rahul: add router cost-model hook + add unit tests (owner)
- sophia: add perf dashboards for attn kernel vs KV-layout (owner)
- liam: open follow-up with kernel team about fused_flash_v2 gather patterns (owner)
anya: noted. will post interim results in this thread and attach plots. expected first batch ~40 minutes.
liam: thanks. ping me if you need raw traces (I recorded nvprof slices).
sophia: :thumbsup: good triage, seems fixable without rolling back the routing change.
rahul: preemptive question — should we add an automated smoke that runs small matrix on canary infra after routing changes? catch regressions early.
liam: yes, add a lightweight canary that tests 3 shapes (short, medium, long) with interleaved vs separate KV toggles. keep it < 5 min.
ci-bot: Canary job created: canary/attn-routing/quick-check
anya: first results uploaded: s3://perf-redwood/attn-layout/matrix-2026-03-17.csv. attaching quick chart in thread in 10m.
liam: received CSV. initial plot shows fused_flash_v2 wins for dim>=128, but separate-kv wins for dim<=64. page_size 32 behaves slightly better than 64 for interleaved.
rahul: perfect. i'll land router heuristic and a flag to force separate-kv for those low-dim shapes. we can later replace with learned model.
sophia: please include a changelog note in release notes: "routing: add KV-layout-aware kernel routing; mitigates medium-sequence latency regression". minimal user-facing impact.
liam: will do. closing loop once router patch lands and canary passes.
anya: uploading final plots now. cc @kernel-team for follow-up.
ci-bot: PR #4135 merged (routing heuristics). Canary quick-check passed. Job: canary/attn-routing/quick-check.
liam: great, thanks everyone. follow-up: kernel team ticket created: KT-2245 (investigate fused_flash v2 interleaved gather).
sophia: thanks — good cross-team flow.
